unresolved: Architectural pottery kiln sites and production organisation are almost entirely absent: 'thousands of tile kilns south of Duling' is a Sanguozhi quotation written after the Han emperor it describes, and 'state pottery kilns along the Wei River' is one sentence; beyond these there are no kiln names, owners, craftsmen, output, cost or sales records

Tile and brick dimensions survive as three isolated examples and do not form a specification series: Western Zhou flat tile 40 x 20 x 1.3 cm, Qin mausoleum tile end about 40 cm diameter, square brick 'about 42 high and 48 wide' as a type norm. The glazed-tile 'ten grades' (B.5.4) is the only sequenced specification in the library; brick and tile have none, so standardisation cannot be judged

The separation of tile nail from tile body is a single sentence with no before/after forms, connection method, strength data or date. The same book writes 'nails and rings' in one place and 'nails or rings' in another; whether both existed and how they divided work is unstated

Tile-end mold-pressing is described only as 'mold-impression method' (Gao Feng): no mold material, single-piece or multi-piece forming, trimming or luting, and no data on mold reuse or wear against motif consistency. The Warring States 'more than 30 kinds' is a type count, not output or distribution

Two incompatible classifications of Han tile-end motifs coexist and are not merged: Gao Feng's pictorial / text / text-with-pictorial three-way split and Tian Zibing's cloud, animal, four-divinity and text four-way split are not refinements of one standard. Tian's four-way split is the only one, and the claim that 'most are auspicious phrases' is an evaluation, not a count; Li Lixin's ideological explanation is never attached to a single tile end

The directional quality of tile ends rests on one sentence from Zhao Nong with no instances or direction-to-motif table; the four-divinity/direction correspondence comes from a general passage in the same book, not from tile-end evidence. Whether the Yanxiadu fu-fu patterned large tiles and the 'one-metre' giant impressed tile ends are the same batch is unstated

Image bricks have only the type norm for square bricks as a dimension; the counts 'more than 70 kinds' (Tian Zibing) and 'more than 80' (Gao Feng) coexist without a stated basis, and all seven concrete objects lack size, thickness, tomb attribution and collection. The hollow brick's three functional claims (easy to fire, light, moisture-proof) have no wall thickness, cavity size or firing temperature data; 'sealing clay slabs at both ends with one hole each' is the only venting description, with no hole position, diameter or thickness

The sequence of colouring on image bricks appears only for Dengxian ('after firing, colour was applied to part of the picture, on some up to seven colours'); the seven colour names are unrecorded and the other six bricks' colouring and its timing are unstated. Gao Feng's 'low relief with colour and incised line' versus Dengxian's 'colouring after firing' may or may not be the same process; Gao says the picture was incised into a wooden board in advance while Tian says an incised mould was over-printed, and Gao also lists an 'incised line' method, so the relation between incised mould and incised line is unexplained

The brick painting is described in one sentence as assembled from 'more than 200 bricks'; there is no information on each brick's picture unit, assembly order, numbering, joint treatment or overall wall size, and 'more than 200' cannot establish one picture per brick. The source's evaluation ('a masterpiece of pottery craft ... a new stage') is a stage judgement, not process data

The Seven Sages of the Bamboo Grove has two records: one as a Jin-dynasty caption with no find site (cited by Xia Yanjing 2016 for dress history), one as three Six Dynasties find sites (Zhao Nong). They are probably the same object recorded twice with incompatible dates; the batch mounts only the latter and logs the former as a duplicate candidate for reconcile

The shift of brick from facing to arch construction is a library interpretation, not a source conclusion: Zhao Nong separately records Western Zhou solid bricks used as wall facing and Han wedge/tenon bricks for arch tops, several centuries apart with no intermediate material, and no book connects them into a change of structural role

The division of labour between B.5.4 and B.5.6 over glazed tiles has not been tested against the sources: B.5.4 takes the glaze surface, B.5.6 takes the body and component form, so the same tile is drawn on twice. This is the library's own partition, not a distinction the sources make, and must be re-examined when B.5 is reviewed as a whole

The naming direction of the tile motif (wa-wen) is unrecorded: Tian Zibing only says it consists of parallel bands 'like roof tiles', without saying whether the motif took its name from the tile or giving the chronological order of tile and motif. B.5.6 uses it only to show that tile coursing was a visible formal reference in the Zhou, and does not infer the direction of naming
notes: 本批新建 1 个 Topic（B.5.6 建筑用陶），挂载 13 个 KU，不新增 Theme。结构设计的三项判断：其一，原定 Topic 名「建筑用陶与画像砖」把构件与图像两类并列，读完 13 条候选后改判为「建筑用陶：屋面、砖砌与模印图像」——材料真正回答的是陶器转为构件后同一次成形如何同时满足结构、连接与图像。其二，三层组织：构件端头（瓦当挡椽与装饰是同一构件的两个功能，尺寸由椽径定）、连接件独立化（瓦钉与瓦身分离，六册唯一一条「把一体成形拆成两件」的工艺选择）、模印四尺度（瓦当／方砖／空心砖／砖画，把图像从一次性绘制变成可复制产品）。其三，两条判断：砖的结构角色发生过从贴面到砌拱的转变（标为本库解释框架）；画像砖同时是墙与画，空心砖把结构与图像写在同一段。五处边界处置：琉璃瓦釉面归 B.5.4、胎体归本 Topic；画像砖题材与构图归 C；画像石不在 B.5；瓦纹只取命名事实；竹林七贤两条著录只挂六朝一条。跨维度挂载 7 条（C 主维度 KU 入 B 主题），沿用 D.2.2／D.4.3 既有先例。本批不 commit、不 push。
